newsitem.title: FRANCE: French ex-political boss guilty in sleaze probe.
newsitem.headline: French ex-political boss guilty in sleaze probe.

text.p: Maurice Arreckx. a former Riviera political boss who liked to be called "the Godfather" was condemned on Monday to two years in prison on charges of taking kickbacks in a political sleaze case.
Arreckx, who is 79 and has already spent more than nine months in preventive detention, was also fined one million francs ($200,000) and barred from public office for five years.
Arreckx said he had not yet decided whether he would appeal against the verdict.
"My honour has been rehabilitated, as has that of my family," he told reporters after the verdict.

Arreckx, who was mayor of the Mediterranean port city of Toulon for 26 years until 1985 and also served as the representative of the southern Var department to the French Senate, was accused by prosecutors of extorting 1.8 million francs in return for a construction contract in 1991.
Prosecutor Michel Raffin had recommended at Arreckx's trial in mid-October that he be sentenced to five years in jail and fined one million francs.
